questions.q: Name two mountain ranges that act as northern boundaries for the Peninsular Plateau.
questions.a: The Vindhya and Satpura ranges. A wrong answer suggests the student is confusing northern mountain ranges like the Himalayas with the plateau's specific borders.

questions.q: Why do geologists describe the Peninsular Plateau as an "ancient" landmass?
questions.a: It was formed billions of years ago from very old rocks, whereas the Himalayas are "young" and still rising today. A wrong answer shows the student does not understand the difference between geological time scales.

questions.q: If you were standing in the middle of the Peninsular Plateau, would you expect to see the same tectonic activity found in the Himalayas? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, because the plateau is made of very stable, ancient rock that is no longer rising or shifting significantly. A wrong answer reveals the student doesn't grasp that "ancient" implies structural stability.

questions.q: How do the Western and Eastern Ghats define the shape of the Peninsular Plateau?
questions.a: They act as the western and eastern edges, forming a triangular shape that tapers toward the southern tip of India. A wrong answer indicates the student is not using spatial reasoning to visualize landforms.

questions.q: Is it more accurate to call the Peninsular Plateau a "mountain" or a "tableland"? Justify your choice.
questions.a: It is a tableland because, while it has hills and ranges, its general surface is a raised, flat-topped area. A wrong answer indicates the student is confusing the term "plateau" with "mountain."

questions.q: Imagine India without the Peninsular Plateau. How would the geography of southern India look different?
questions.a: The answer should focus on the lack of a high-altitude central landmass, potentially resulting in a much flatter or submerged southern region. Poor answers fail to connect the plateau to its role as the physical "base" of India.
